sections.text:
This procedure details the steps required to completely
 check the proper operation and calibration of the RAZFE distance relay. It is
 recommended this procedure be carried out on a yearly bases. This work be
 carried out section of this document is divided into 3 sections.

The first preliminary steps to prepare for relay testing
 describes the activities required prior to testing. Some of these steps could
 be performed days before the actual test. The second section Preparation for
 testing describes the steps to set up the equipment for performing the actual
 tests. The third section is the actual test.

The document is formatted the way to minimize the
 possibility of error causing personal injury or damage to equipment.

The first draft 
initialed by eng.
 Saher Farok Mohamed, tested at 22 Aug.1996 at 
 Metro by eng. Saher Farok Mohamed, 
 approved by general director of Protection rng. Maher Gerges.

items:
The characteristic of the power swing relay measuring element is
shown in Fig. 8

Check on printed
 board assembly B11 that the power swing relay programming switch K4 has a
 plug in position 1 or 2. If the plug is in position 3 the power swing relay
 is decommissioned and only p-flag will arrive when testing according to

Set switch F in

 should give signal for Communication send" during the tests above.

Set switch GR and
 potentiometer FR at their highest values and switch Gx and potentiometer
 Fx
 at position 0, i.e. the voltage and the current will be in phase 0.

Turn switch H to
 position I and reduce the setting of GR until the distance relay operates,
 which can be checked by observing the operation of the tripping or
 "power swing" indications of the relay.

Increase GR one step
 and reset the relay and the indicators.

Reduce slowly the
 setting of FR until the "power swing" operates and wait about 2
 seconds. (The tripping indication shall now operate.)

Turn switch H to
 position 0. Read off the values of GR and FR and calculate the operating
 impedance which should be equal to the 100%-line limit in Fig. 8 according
 to the formulas XM & RM are 
 given in the above.

Increase the set
 value of the resistance in the test set to approximately 110 %.

Reduce the setting
 of GR or FR below the operating value obtained in step
 No. (4) of the relay and observe
 the tripping indication of the distance relay. This indication should appear
 approximately 2 sec. after the reduction of the setting. Check that the
 signal for power swing blocking is obtained during the above interval of 2
 sec. as well as "power swing" c blocking indication (P).

Keep GR and
 FR at
 a value below the operating value of the relay and set switch M to position 0
 (full voltage)'. Reset the relay and the indicators.

Turn switch M to
 position 1 (set values of GR and FR) and observe the tripping indication.
 This indication should appear instantaneously but no signial or indication
 for power swing should be obtained.

Make sure that the
 relays which may have been removed from the distance relay in conjunction
 with previous measurement are put back to their respective positions.

The steady-state
 fault conditions for different types of faults can be simulated with the aid
 of relay test set and the total operating time of the relay for different
 steps can then be checked with a separate timer.

Please note that the
 test set does not reproduce the dynamic phenomena.

Insert the test-plug
 handle RTXH 18 in the distance relay. Connect the contact H 2 of the test set
 to obtain simultaneous start of the timer and of the distance relay when
 turning the main switch H to position 1. the tripping pulse from the relay
 is connected to stop the timer

The connection is
 made according to Fig. 2 which applies to a synchronous timer type 51 of
 AEG' s make. When the timer is of the design that can be stopped by D.C supply the stop circuit for the timer is connected directly to the test
 terminal in the trip circuit of the distance relay.

On the other
 hand, the stop circuit of the timer must be insulated, an extra auxiliary
 relay with known operating time should be provided. the trip circuit of the
 distance relay should operate this extra relay.

Set the switch F of
 the test set in position e.g. TR and switch Q in position 1

Set the switches S1,
 S2, GX , GR and potentiometer FX and FR so that
 the "desired impedance" is applied to the relay.

Reset indicators and
 timer.

When the switch H is
 turned in position 1, the desired impedance is applied to the distance relay
 and the starting elements initiate the time-lag relay to operate. When the
 set time of each time-lag relays is up they extend the reach of the distance
 relay. The distance relay gives a tripping impulse when its reach is larger
 than the "impedance" applied by the test set.

In this way the
 operating time of the distance relay can easily be checked for desired type
 of fault and fault position.
 If the time
 measurement is to be utilized for the matching of the settings of the
 time-lag relays to the selectivity plan, it is suggested that the
 measurement should be carried out as follows:

Select the applied
 " impedance" so that it is approximately equal to, but larger
 than, the reach set for the first or
 second step and with phase angle equal to 90 . this is obtained with switch
 GR and potentiometer FR in 0 position.

Perform the time
 measurement test as stated above.

Introduction
This procedure details the steps required to completely

 recommended this procedure be carried out on a yearly bases. This work be

The first preliminary steps to prepare for relay testing

 be performed days before the actual test. The second section Preparation for
 testing describes the steps to set up the equipment for performing the actual

The document is formatted the way to minimize the
 possibility of error causing personal injury or damage to equipment.
